test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 27 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In which year were four new Directive Principles added to the original list?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1976** is the year when four new Directive Principles were added to the original list.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** of 1976 is responsible for this addition.
 
• The new principles included in the amendment were focused on **securing participation of workers in the management of industries, promoting equal justice and free legal aid, protection of environment and wildlife, and promotion of international peace and security.**
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also direct the state to ensure distributive justice and to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all the institutions of national life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are enumerated in **Part IV** of the Constitution of India from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These provisions are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down therein are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The idea of such policies has been borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.
 
• The principles aim to establish social and economic democracy in the country.
 
• Although non-justiciable, the Directive Principles have been used to interpret the scope and ambit of Fundamental Rights in various landmark judgments.
